newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees 1997 as "decisive" fiscal year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees 1997 as "decisive" fiscal year.

text.p: The Brazilian government considers 1997 to be "decisive" in the battle to balance its books and stabilize its growing debt stockpile, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.

Kandir reaffirmed the federal government was committed to achieving a primary budget surplus of 0.8 percent of gross domestic product and a primary surplus for the consolidated public sector accounts of 1.5 percent of GDP.
"The year 1997 is truly decisive (for the government's attempts to balance its books)," Kandir told reporters after a ministerial cabinet meeting called to discuss the 1997 budget.
"The government is determined to pursue a (federal) primary surplus of 0.8 percent of GDP," the minister said.

In the same briefing, presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said state firms were expected to post a primary surplus of 0.7 percent of GDP and that the states would hopefully end the year in fiscal balance, generating a primary suplus of 1.5 percent for the consolidated public sector.

In 1996, the public sector saw a small primary deficit of 0.08 percent of GDP. In operational terms, which unlike the primary result includes debt servicing costs, the public sector posted a 3.89 percent of GDP deficit.
Kandir said the cabinet had approved the bimonthly spending programme outlined in the 1997 budget and that financial discipline would help achieve the government's fiscal results.
He said 85 percent of funds allocated to the ministries were guaranteed and that the remaining 15 percent would be freed up depending on the performance of tax revenue.

Of 9.8 billion reais in total first half income budgeted for the ministries, 8.3 billion reais was guaranteed. In the second half, 14.5 billion had been allocated to the ministries of which 10.5 billion was guaranteed.
The rest depended on revenue and also on approval by Congress of the Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF), a key fiscal tool that allows the government to spend some of the budget as it sees fit.
Kandir said 1.9 billion reais in budgeted revenue for the ministries depended on the FEF.
"Let me state quite clearly," Kandir said. "We don't expect a shortfall in tax revenue as our estimates...are extremely conservative."
